scope: Reviewed the implemented Part 1 decoding subset against ITU-T T.800 (06/2019), local itu-t800-2019.txt: Annex A marker syntax and placement; B.1-B.12 grids, partitions, packets and progressions; C.3 and Table C.2 arithmetic decoding; D.1-D.7 coefficient modelling and termination; E.1 dequantization; F.2-F.3 synthesis; G.1-G.4 level shift, component transforms and sampling; H.1 ROI; I.3-I.5 and I.8 JP2 boxes. Per-requirement verdicts distinguish agreement, corrected disagreements, documented choices and explicit unsupported subsets; this is not complete format conformance certification. PDF permissions and dictionary contracts remain checked against ISO 32000-2 EC3 7.4.9 and 8.9.5 Table 87. Only Part 2 extension semantics (T.801), ICC profile conformance (ISO 15076-1/ICC.1) and external colour definitions remain pending primary-text review; their bytes/identifiers are preserved without colour conversion. Coding-pass prefix reconstruction is additionally verified against D.2.1/D.3, E-6-E-8 and H.1, with packet-boundary incomplete final volumes under B.10/B.12.3; no physical missing-byte repair is implied.

differential_evidence.kind: supporting differential evidence; normative verdicts come from primary text
differential_evidence.results: 100 comparisons pass: exact reversible results and irreversible differences at most 2 within declared tolerances 1 or 3. Five text-derived decoder cases disagree, listed separately. Six ICC/opacity/CMYK metadata cases and the 257-component POC case use independent sample/metadata assertions rather than comparable colour-managed PNM output.

disagreements.observed: OpenJPEG rejects PPT indices restarted per header; T.800 A.7.5 scopes the index to the current header.
OpenJPEG sample differences 131 and 15 respectively; T.800 D.6 starts bypass after four significant bit-planes without an ROI-dependent delay.
OpenJPEG rejects nonzero unused exponent/padding bits; A.1.3 prescribes ignoring unused bits even though conforming encoders must write zero.

choices: E.1 reconstruction parameter r=1/2; irreversible output rounded to nearest integer and clipped to sample endpoints.
I.5.3.4 leaves out-of-table palette index handling unspecified; endpoint clamping is retained.
A.7.4/A.7.5 fragment indices are sorted by value; gaps are accepted, duplicate indices rejected.
Standalone raw codestream support does not establish the PDF full-file requirement.
Limits are conservative cumulative allocation/work policies, not format limits.

fault_decisions.fault: tile-part count records the last index rather than the number of parts
fault_decisions.verdict: Malformed: TNsot=5 cannot describe indices 0 through 5. Retain positioned Syntax. A bounded off-by-one recovery would require Recovery/Diagnostics at the codec boundary and an explicit repair tag under ADR 0003; no silent recovery.

fault_decisions.fault: PDF Indexed colour space with one codestream component mapped through a four-column JP2 palette
fault_decisions.verdict: The ordinary channel count after cmap is four, while PDF Indexed requires one input component. Retain the image facade mismatch error. Ignoring colr does not erase cmap channel definitions; choosing the PDF palette over the embedded palette would be a reported recovery requiring image-layer changes.

partial_quality_evidence.oracle: Coefficient prefixes from T.800 D.3/Table D.6; coefficient-specific E-6/E-8 midpoints; H.1 ROI realignment; zero-detail F.3.8.1 interpolation. Expected samples are computed independently of Rust and of decoder output.
partial_quality_evidence.rust: Exact agreement with every new sample oracle, including irreversible prefix cases.
partial_quality_evidence.openjpeg: OpenJPEG 2.5.4 supports the normative review: 135 exact comparisons; two single-sample differences of one on partial-irreversible-9 and partial-irreversible-10. These are the existing signed coefficient tie-rounding choice before level shifting, not a change to fixture tolerances.
partial_quality_evidence.rounding_choice: Choose r=1/2; round reconstructed signed coefficients to nearest integer, ties away from zero, then level shift and clip. Reversible E-8 produces exact integer midpoints.

performance_evidence.profile: An 846 x 1103 three-component, five-level irreversible image charges 82,966,761 work units before correction: 59,684,688 for wavelet synthesis, 2,555,246 for coefficient pass scans. Diagnostic phase timing measured about 17 ms in synthesis of about 58 ms total; system sampling was unavailable, so phase timers and budget attribution were used.
performance_evidence.cause: The fixed 16-units-per-sample synthesis estimate exceeds the actual coefficient traversals. Two standalone scaling traversals and a second tier-1 coefficient allocation are also unnecessary.
performance_evidence.change: Fuse row scaling into subband interleaving and column scaling into the existing gather. Preserve the order of every floating-point multiplication and lift. Charge seven coefficient visits per synthesis sample (three copies, plus four lifting/range-check visits), with allocation initialization charged separately. Return coefficient state directly rather than copying it to an i64 vector.
performance_evidence.limits: The default 50,000,000 operation limit and every allocation/pixel limit remain unchanged. Dense or larger images may still exceed these limits.
performance_evidence.code_delta: Wavelet implementation: 23 lines added, 7 removed. Tier-1 direct return removes a five-line allocation/conversion sequence (replaced by one direct return); the per-coefficient prefix counter fits the existing sample-state padding. Prefix correctness changes are separate from the optimization.
performance_evidence.alternatives: A strided in-place column experiment was slower and was discarded. No context cache, threading, architecture-specific code or increased resource limit was added.
performance_evidence.equivalence: 94 previously supported real-file codestreams and 125 generated codestream/container vectors compare identical in all returned samples and metadata, under the same diagnostic resource allowance.

measurement.case: One 846 x 1103 irreversible synthesis level with dense LL and zero high bands; identical optimized Rust build for both implementations. Five alternating pairs of 60 iterations. Child user+system CPU time avoids host scheduling delay; startup/input setup is included in both sides.
measurement.scope: Native synthesis microbenchmark, not an end-to-end renderer speed claim.

performance_evidence.remaining_dense_case: A real-world image of 1394 x 1058 RGB with dense coded coefficients: 184,456,854 units before and 126,971,331 after. Even the corrected accounting exceeds the unchanged 50,000,000 cap; the limit remains explicit.

realworld_validation.method: All 1000 corpus files scanned at 72 dpi (998 PDF headers). Initial harness used 60 CPU seconds per document. Native uncapped rescans completed 0315, 0522 and 0888; two pre-existing timeouts remain excluded. Product Limits unchanged.
realworld_validation.comparison: Each document/page success set was compared, rather than only comparing totals. Three harness timeouts were completed with the native scan command; the two original timeouts remain excluded. No product Limits were raised.
